target_customer: At YC time, crypto companies and DAOs needing accounting (as Coinbooks); later LLM app developers needing security; now insurers and financial institutions buying AI agents
problem: Crypto-native teams could not reconcile wallet activity with normal accounting software; the company later moved to securing LLM apps and then to enterprise AI agents for insurance and finance operations.
business_model: B2B software subscription and custom enterprise deployments
product_category: Enterprise AI agents (earlier: DAO accounting, LLM security)

founders.name: Arnav Bathla
founders.background_notes: YC page says he has shipped products since age 13 and won the NSS space settlement contest three times. The Block (March 2022) calls him 21 years old, but a birth year is not stated so no age is recorded. Education not stated on pages opened.

competitors.name: Request Finance
competitors.what: Crypto invoicing and payroll for crypto companies, adjacent to accounting
competitors.funding_then: $5.5M seed, June 2022 (a few months after the Coinbooks raise)

technical_complexity.rationale: Wallet and on-chain data ingestion and mapping to accounting systems is standard engineering with some chain-specific hard parts; the later LLM and agent products are moderately complex.

defensibility.rationale: Several funded crypto accounting rivals existed and LLM security guardrails were quickly copied by open source and larger vendors.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Kruze Consulting reported in January 2023 that Coinbooks was going to stop serving startups, unverified; the company later pivoted and now sells agentic AI.

market_need_then: Existing accounting platforms integrate with bank accounts, not wallets (founder quote in The Block, March 2022), and DAOs were multiplying during the 2021 to 2022 crypto boom.

branding.domain_note: Company uses uselayerup.com, a prefix domain, not an exact .com.

identity.voice_and_tone: Enterprise and technical, 'autonomous operations, governed by your enterprise'

rebrands.why: Not stated; CB Insights and Craft list Layerup as also known as Coinbooks, and the date of the change was not found.

branding.community_and_virality: Founder story of a young dropout raising $3.2M was covered by The Block, Forbes headline listed on the YC page and Indian outlets; none about the Layerup brand itself.

brand_strength.rationale: Little press on the brand, a prefix domain and a name that changed with each pivot.

pivots.from: LLM security and legal compliance platform
pivots.to: Agentic AI for financial services and insurance
pivots.why: Not stated; inferred from changing company positioning only

outcome_analysis: The company raised $3.2M as Coinbooks in early 2022 before YC Summer 2022, then changed direction to LLM security and later to enterprise AI agents for insurers. It is still listed as active with a team of 11, but sources are thin and do not show revenue or later priced rounds, so success is not established.
notes: Identification of Layerup with Coinbooks rests on CB Insights and Craft listing Layerup as also known as Coinbooks plus the Forbes headline on the YC page; the YC page does not state it. Rounds come from The Block and Crowdfund Insider about Coinbooks. Aggregators report $125K seed, a $0.5M convertible note in September 2022 and about $3.7M to $4M total; these are unverified and not recorded as rounds. Request Finance seed is dated June 2022, after the Coinbooks raise, noted as within months of the batch.
